plan.title: doctor writes xbrief/.triage-cache/doctor-state.json on every full run (AC12.1)

narratives.Description: OVPR fix plan group G-F (story id ovpr-g-doctor): P3-U2 + P4-U3c + P5-U1b + O-29, issues #6617, #6618, #6622, #5967 items 1-3, #6004. Doctor must write nothing (AC12.1) and tell the truth. Doctor stops writing xbrief/.triage-cache/doctor-state.json (the time window moves into session start's .deft/orientation-state.json); the `--fix` / `--repair` / `--repair-taskfile` write paths are removed; doctor warns read-only when a Directive file that must be committed is hidden by an ignore rule; the #6300 `directive update --allow-dirty-no-stage` advice goes; gitignore coverage expects exactly the RC-05 named AC8.5 list (setup adds the runtime-file lines) with remedy `directive install --repair`; the Taskfile check accepts the runtime include and never teaches `.deft/core`; chooseRemedy names one next command per failure class from the message table; `--json` prints one JSON document; the headline tracks the worst result; absent is 'not present', not 'ok'; pnpm's own dangling links are a warning.
narratives.Overview:
## Problem

`directive doctor` is meant to only look, never change anything. In fact it writes a small state file into the project every time it runs a full check. In a customer project that file is not ignored. After running doctor, `git status` shows a new file, and `git add -A` commits it. Two customer reports show this (#6006, #5999).

Evidence (origin/master `def527f5e`):
- The write: `packages/core/src/doctor/main.ts:1172-1179` calls `persist(...)` (`seams.writeState ?? writeState`) after every full run. `writeState` (`packages/core/src/doctor/doctor-state.ts:59`) writes `xbrief/.triage-cache/doctor-state.json`.
- The launcher path reaches it: `directive doctor` → `runDoctor` (`packages/cli/src/bookends.ts:1662`, whose comment at `:1660` says "Never writes") → runtime contract `doctor` → `cmdDoctor` → the write.
- Why it writes: a rate limit (#1315), with two readers.
  1. `cmdDoctor` without `--full` (`main.ts:716` onward) skips only when a live `.deft/core` exists (`:720`, #4723 / #4886). **An OVPR project has no `.deft/core`, so on an OVPR project doctor writes the file and never uses it.**
  2. Session start: `runDoctorOrientationSection` (`packages/core/src/session/orientation-compression.ts:210`) reads it with `decideThrottle` (`:231`). This is the only live use on OVPR projects.
- Session start already keeps its own record in `.deft/orientation-state.json` (`OrientationState.doctor`, `packages/core/src/session/orientation-state.ts:32`).
- Why trees get dirty: OVPR setup adds only two ignore lines (`packages/runtime/src/setup.ts:166-168`), as AC8.5 says. `xbrief/.triage-cache/doctor-state.json` is only in the legacy baseline (`packages/core/src/init-deposit/gitignore.ts:122`), which OVPR setup never writes.

## What the design says

- AC12.1: "Doctor writes no files and runs no installs in any state. … Snapshot the project, relevant Git configuration and isolated global location before/after diagnostic tests." Writing to a user cache instead would also fail this.
- AC8.8 / AC9.10: plain doctor never triggers setup; every doctor child suppresses installation writes.
- LLM-CONTEXT §3 verb matrix and locked rule 5: doctor is read-only.
- AC8.5: only the `node_modules` and readiness-marker ignore lines are added.
- D-001 (Rule 1): doctor stops writing `doctor-state.json`.
- O-28 (RC-05, default OK): session start keeps its timestamp in `.deft/orientation-state.json`. Whether that file is ignored is RC-05.

## Expected

1. Remove the `persist(...)` call in `main.ts`. Remove the throttle-skip branch in `cmdDoctor` (it only fires on `.deft/core` projects, which the launcher already turns away with "Run `directive upgrade`"). Keep `--full` as an accepted flag with no effect, because the launcher forwards it.
2. Move the time window into session start. `runDoctorOrientationSection` decides skip from `readOrientationState(root)?.doctor` (the time doctor last actually ran, and its exit code), with the same `decideThrottle` windows. A skipped section carries the previous `doctor` record forward unchanged; a new `ts` is stamped only when doctor actually ran. With `--read-only`, session start writes nothing.
3. One-time compatibility: if `xbrief/.triage-cache/doctor-state.json` exists and there is no `orientation-state.doctor`, session start may read it once. Doctor never deletes it (AC12.1). Uninstall lists it as a known leftover (hand to the #5999 lane).
4. Remove `writeState` from `doctor-state.ts` and its export from `doctor/index.ts`. Update the tests that call it (`doctor-state-write.test.ts`, `doctor-state.test.ts`, `main-branches.test.ts`, `coverage-final.test.ts`, `triage/cache-path.test.ts`).
5. Add an AC12.1 test: run `cmdDoctor` and the contract `doctor` entry on a fixture; snapshot every project file and `.git/config` before and after; assert no change. Run git probes with `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`.

Must not do: don't move the state file to a user cache or temp directory; don't add `xbrief/.triage-cache/` or any other line to the consumer `.gitignore` to hide the symptom ("fix the write, not `.gitignore`"); don't add any `--fix` or auto-repair.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Running `directive doctor` and `directive doctor --full` on an OVPR fixture leaves every project file, `.git/config` and `.git/index` byte-identical.
2. Doctor never creates `xbrief/.triage-cache/doctor-state.json`.
3. Session start still skips the doctor run when doctor ran less than 24 h (clean) or 4 h (failing) ago, using `.deft/orientation-state.json`. A skipped run does not extend the window.
4. All new git probes are read-only and run with `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`.

Verification: `pnpm vitest run packages/core/src/doctor packages/core/src/session`; on a scratch OVPR clone, `git status --porcelain` is identical before and after `directive doctor --full`; `task check` on the PR.

## Related

- #6006, #5999: the `doctor-state.json` part is fixed here; the rest of each ticket stays open. Comment on both when this merges.
- #4673 (closed): the 22 h throttle surprise, same mechanism.
- #6618: the hidden-file warning and the #6300 advice fix (same unit, second PR).
- #6622: removes doctor's `--fix` write paths, which this ticket leaves alone.

## Plan placement

- Unit P3-U2, Part A (P3-U2a), story id `ovpr-p3-u2`. Phase 3, wave 3.1. Size M for the whole unit.
- Depends on: nothing. Can ship before Part B.
- Owner polfer.
narratives.UserStory: As a developer running directive doctor, I want doctor to change nothing in my project, to name exactly one correct next command for each problem, and to give honest, parseable output, so that I can trust its verdict and script against it.

Read all three in full; 'Update' banners win. RC-05 (drafts/RC-05.md) is approved and merged: it settles P3-U2 Q7a/Q7b and P5-U1b Q1 (the named .gitignore list). RC-06 is merged: use its wording via the G-G (P4-U3a) message table.

AC12.1 snapshot test (project files, .git/config, .git/index; GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0).
O-29 (#6622): 5. Remove every doctor write path under fixMode: Taskfile create in main.ts, OpenClaw pin install (openclaw-skills.ts), soft re-bind deposit (openclaw-soft-rebind.ts), L2 skills (openclaw-l2-adapter.ts); packages/core/src/doctor/flags.ts. Part C + RC-05: 7. packages/core/src/doctor/checks.ts: delete GITIGNORE_DIRTY_TREE_FIX / GITIGNORE_DIRTY_TREE_RECOVERY / data.dirty_tree_fix; gitignore-coverage expects the RC-05 AC8.5 list (node_modules/, .deft/directive/wiring-ready.*.json, .deft/pre-pr-execution-private/, .deft/plan-sequence.json.generation, .deft/plan-sequence.json.lock, .deft/plan-sequence.json.lock.claim-*, .deft/orientation-state.json) with remedy `directive install --repair`; other legacy baseline lines are information only; pre-pr-secret-tracked text matches. packages/runtime/src/setup.ts ensureGitignore adds the RC-05 runtime-file lines (runtime setup, not the launcher).

narratives.Constraint:
- Doctor writes nothing anywhere under any flag (AC12.1): no state file in the project, user cache or temp dir; no git config or ignore-file writes; no new --fix or auto-repair.
- Do not add xbrief/.triage-cache/ or any line outside the RC-05 named list to the consumer .gitignore. Only runtime setup adds the RC-05 runtime-file lines; the launcher does not (AC3.3).
- Do not suggest `npm i -g` + repair or `upgrade` for an ignore-rule problem; never print --allow-dirty-no-stage; never name `directive update` as the remedy for ignore lines (AC12.7).
- Recovery wording comes from the G-G (P4-U3a) message table and RC-06 text; do not invent new recovery strings. Do not change WIRING_RECOVERY_GUIDANCE or the no-git remedy.
- Keep exit-code meaning, except the dangling-link downgrade (fail -> warning for pnpm's own links).
- Do not touch verify:consumer-check-contract (#5967 item 4, Scott).
- O-29: stop and report before removing a write path that has no other owner, and before deciding usage-error vs no-op for --fix/--repair/--repair-taskfile (#6622).
- chooseRemedy() is also edited by G-D (foreign hooksPath branch); keep the two changes mergeable.
- OVPR change gate: read ~/Projects/directive-ovpr-planning-202611/OVPR-CHANGE-GATE.md. Do not edit docs/installer-refactor-ovpr/ and do not ship behaviour that departs from the written OVPR requirements or architecture; stop that part and hand back a change proposal.
- Changelog: add the changelog.d fragment named in file_scope; never edit CHANGELOG.md.

P2-U0 ownership API (listDirectiveOwnedPaths) is merged (#6658). RC-05 and RC-06 docs are merged. Part A (#6617) has no dependency and can land first. Coordinate with G-D (doctor-diagnose.ts chooseRemedy, setup.ts) and G-E (bookends.ts).

items.title: Running `directive doctor` and `directive doctor --full` on an OVPR fixture leaves every project file, `.git/config` and `.git/index` byte-identical.

narrative.Acceptance: Given an OVPR fixture, when `directive doctor` and `directive doctor --full` run, then every project file, .git/config and .git/index are byte-identical before and after (AC12.1 snapshot test).
Given an OVPR fixture without xbrief/.triage-cache/doctor-state.json, when doctor runs, then that file does not exist afterwards.

items.title: Session start still skips the doctor run inside the window (24 h clean, 4 h failing) using `.deft/orientation-state.json`; a skipped run does not extend the window.

narrative.Acceptance: Given an orientation-state doctor record 1 h old with exit 0, when session start runs, then doctor is not run and the record's ts is unchanged; given a record 25 h old, when session start runs, then doctor runs and a new record is stamped.

items.title: `deft doctor --fix`, `--repair` and `--repair-taskfile` write nothing: no Taskfile, no OpenClaw pins, no skills (O-29 / #6622).

narrative.Acceptance: Given a fixture with a missing Taskfile.yml and missing OpenClaw pins, when `deft doctor --fix`, `--repair` and `--repair-taskfile` run, then the project, .git/config and the isolated global location are byte-identical, and no write path remains under fixMode in packages/core/src/doctor.

items.title: With `.cursor/` in `.git/info/exclude`, `directive doctor` warns naming the hidden `.cursor/hooks/deft-hook-<sha8>.mjs` and `.git/info/exclude:<line>`, and its exit code is unchanged.

narrative.Acceptance: Given `.cursor/` in .git/info/exclude, when `directive doctor` runs, then it prints the directive-files-hidden warning naming the .mjs path and `.git/info/exclude:<line>`, and the exit code equals the run without that rule.

items.title: A global excludes file is named the same way; a `!` negation gives no warning; skip-worktree on `.claude/settings.json` warns; an ignored readiness marker gives no warning.

narrative.Acceptance: Given core.excludesFile in a temporary HOME hiding an owned file, a `!` negation rule, skip-worktree on .claude/settings.json, and an ignored readiness marker, when doctor runs, then the first and third warn with their source, and the negation and readiness marker give no warning.

items.title: Gitignore coverage expects exactly the RC-05 named AC8.5 list, with remedy `directive install --repair`; setup adds the runtime-file lines; no doctor output contains `--allow-dirty-no-stage` or names `directive update` / `upgrade` for an ignore line.

narrative.Acceptance: Given an OVPR project with an exact pin and only the RC-05 named lines, when doctor runs, then gitignore coverage does not warn; given one named line missing, then the remedy is `directive install --repair`; and given runtime setup on a fresh project, then .gitignore gains the RC-05 runtime-file lines; no doctor output contains `--allow-dirty-no-stage` or advises update/upgrade for an ignore line.

items.title: On an upgraded fixture whose Taskfile includes the runtime Taskfile, doctor reports no Gates-surface include warning, and no doctor output or snippet contains `.deft/core/Taskfile.yml`.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a Taskfile including ./node_modules/@deftai/directive-runtime/Taskfile.yml, when doctor runs, then there is no include warning; given a `.deft/core` include, then the status is legacy-include with the wiring-damaged row; and no output or snippet contains `.deft/core/Taskfile.yml`.

items.title: For each failure class (installed != pin, runtime missing, pin invalid, lockfile disagrees, GENERATION missing, readiness missing) doctor prints exactly one next command matching the message table; no runtime doctor remedy contains `npm i -g @deftai/directive, then`.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a fixture for each failure class, when the runtime doctor runs, then it prints exactly one next command equal to that class's message-table row, and no remedy contains `npm i -g @deftai/directive, then`.

items.title: For a stale node_modules, `directive doctor` (launcher) and the runtime doctor (via `task doctor`) print the same next command (#5967 AC 3).

narrative.Acceptance: Given a stale node_modules, when `directive doctor` and `task doctor` run, then both print the same next command.

items.title: `directive doctor --json` and `directive doctor --full --json` write exactly one JSON document to stdout in every state (healthy, unhealthy, runtime missing, pin != installed), including install_sync and the product findings; exit codes unchanged.

narrative.Acceptance: Given each of those four states, when `directive doctor --json` and `--full --json` run, then stdout parses with one JSON.parse and contains install_sync, contract, dataStatus and findings, and the exit code matches today's.

items.title: Human doctor output never shows `directive doctor: in sync` or `OK` as the overall verdict when any section reports an error.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a healthy install sync and a product suite with errors, when `directive doctor` runs, then the final overall line is 'problems found', not 'in sync' or 'OK'.

items.title: When no host hook configs or skill pointers exist, doctor shows 'not present', not 'ok'; the default hook probe shows 'not probed'.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a project with no host hook configs and no skill pointers, when doctor runs, then those rows read 'not present' and the default hook probe reads 'not probed'.

items.title: A dangling link under `node_modules/.pnpm/` gives a warning, not an error; a dangling Directive package link still fails.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a dangling link at node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/foo, when doctor runs, then it is a warning; given a dangling node_modules/@deftai/directive-runtime, then it is a fail.

items.title: All new git probes are read-only and run with `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`; `git status` is unchanged after `directive doctor`.

narrative.Acceptance: Given the doctor git probes, when they run, then each runs with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 and `git status --porcelain` is identical before and after `directive doctor`.
